scope: Visual and usability precedents only; no proprietary geometry is copied.

sources.lesson: Expose the work surface and appliance access so the module reads as usable in its deployed state.
Use clear drawer hierarchy, durable latches, and deployable work surfaces within one cabinet volume.
A fridge concept needs a visible low slide tray, positive restraint, ventilation, and lid access.
Contrasting work zones and exposed controls make a compact camp kitchen understandable at a glance.
Drawer fronts need visible pulls, positive latches, and enough separation to communicate independent storage zones.
Robust drawer slides, full-width fronts, and simple rectilinear sheet parts support field-serviceable storage.
Repeated slots and distinct anchors must be visible for a panel or cargo net to read as functional retention hardware.
Sink, stove, storage, and preparation surfaces should be visually separated into a coherent task sequence.
